races.name: Discover Newmarket Fillies' Novice Stakes (GBB Race)
Racing Welfare Novice Stakes (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Livemore
runners_data.note: Hold-up operator trained by T J Kent, 47 days off the track, sole prior run a fifth over 8f on good — the step to a mile is logical but this pace shape is the worst possible setup for a horse who needs genuine fractions to close into.|

runners_data.name: Parc Dosne
runners_data.note: Matt Crawley-trained hold-up type whose best two runs came over 10f, making this mile trip shorter than ideal; showed nothing over soft last time and a steady Newmarket gallop will not generate the late pace he needs to pick up.|

runners_data.name: Vastern
runners_data.note: Lightly raced and stylistically uncertain (U), Pat Cosgrave's mount finished second over 7f on good on sole start — the unknown ceiling makes him a genuine threat if he can sit close enough to Cerro Blanco to pounce in the straight.|

runners_data.name: Anncanya
runners_data.note: Debut runner for Peter Chapple-Hyam with David Probert aboard, going unknown and no form to assess — the complete wildcard in the field, but Chapple-Hyam's novice debutants are always worth monitoring and the unknown style could mean she races prominently by default.|

runners_data.name: La Mariposa
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer whose natural style is to race from the rear, but with the hold-up slots overcrowded she will likely race in a midfield position that is neither natural nor optimal; her two runs in similar going yielded a fifth and an eighth, and Liam Wright (5) rides.|

runners_data.name: Cerro Blanco
runners_data.note: Charlie Appleby's sole front-runner in the race and the clear pace anchor; his form reads 1-2 over 7f on good ground and he steps up to a mile, which on breeding looks like a positive — the lack of any pace rival means he controls every tempo decision in this race.|

runners_data.name: El Carrusel
runners_data.note: Long-absent (253 days off the track) hold-up horse for John Ryan whose last five runs include two on the all-weather and a variety of going types — his genuine style is from the rear, yet he too is squeezed into a midfield slot by the crowded hold-up contingent, and the combination of rustiness and positional mismatch makes him a very tough sell.|

races.paceDynamic: Cerro Blanco is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-runner novice and, with no rival likely to seriously dispute the lead, Billy Loughnane can dictate a controlled, unhurried gallop from the front over this mile on good ground. The pace will almost certainly be steady to modest in the early stages, which compresses the field and drastically reduces the premium on coming from behind — horses held up last will need an unusually strong finishing burst to bridge a gap that was never truly opened up. Vastern and Anncanya are unknown quantities stylistically, but with Livemore, Parc Dosne, La Mariposa, and El Carrusel all natural hold-up or rear-of-field types, the race shape overwhelmingly favours horses that can track close to Cerro Blanco and produce a short, punchy effort from a handy position in the straight. La Mariposa and El Carrusel are genuine hold-up horses mapped forward only because the map's rear positions are saturated — they are unlikely to find their natural ground-saving berth, and this steady pace will not create the late-race gaps they need.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Cerro Blanco Controls Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If Cerro Blanco is allowed to bowl along at a measured pace and the hold-up contingent fail to close the gap in time.
scenarios.body: Loughnane dictates every fraction on a fair gallop, turns for home full of running, and the field's lack of a genuine pace challenger means closers face an uphill task against a horse who never emptied his tank; Cerro Blanco's two prior wins on good ground at 7f suggest stepping up to a mile suits and he has the class edge on OR.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Handy Tracker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Vastern or Anncanya, racing prominently on unknown or lightly-raced form, track Cerro Blanco closely and produce a superior turn of foot in the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: A steady pace suits horses close enough to pounce from second or third, and both Vastern (second on sole start at 7f good) and Anncanya (debut wildcard) are unexposed types whose ceiling is genuinely unknown; the lightly-raced angle gives them an upside that the more exposed hold-up horses cannot match.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Late Surge
scenarios.trigger: If Cerro Blanco sets a faster gallop than expected or capitulates inside the final furlong, allowing hold-up horses to close.
scenarios.body: A genuine acceleration phase would compress the field's finishing positions and give Livemore or Parc Dosne a brief window, though both are unproven at a mile and the flat, steady topology of this race makes a true pace collapse unlikely; Livemore has the best sim-going record among the rear-runners but is 47 days off the track.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Rank Outsider Shocks
scenarios.trigger: If the race is run unusually badly by the market leaders and El Carrusel or La Mariposa, racing out of their natural hold-up roles, stumble into a position that suits.
scenarios.body: Both are redistributed hold-up horses who cannot realistically replicate their best form from the midfield slot they are likely to occupy, and El Carrusel's 253-day absence adds a significant unknown; this scenario requires multiple things to go wrong simultaneously for the principals.

watchPoints.text: Cerro Blanco's gallop tempo is the single biggest variable — if Loughnane eases off dramatically on the good ground, it turns the race into a sprint and lifts every hold-up horse's chance.
Vastern and Anncanya are both lightly raced with stylistic unknowns — if either breaks sharply and tracks Cerro Blanco from the gate, they become the primary threats given their unexposed upside.

La Mariposa and El Carrusel are natural hold-up horses racing out of role in a midfield position; watch for them to drift back to their comfort zone early, which would leave them with too much ground to make up in a pace-controlled race.
El Carrusel's 253-day layoff is a serious flag — watch for any signs of market drift or yard confidence signals pre-race given John Ryan's T14 return of just 1/6.

The going is officially unknown at Newmarket (July) — any late ground update before the off could shift the dynamic, particularly for Parc Dosne who showed poor form on soft and whose profile improves sharply on faster surfaces.

races.name: Racing TV Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: Patrol
runners_data.note: Front-runner by trade who sets the tone here on good ground over a trip that stretches him (his best form has been at 1m2f); Dylan Cunha's yard is winless in 15 runners over 14 days, and while Patrol's similar-going form is modest (0W2P), the absence of pace rivals is a significant tactical gift.

runners_data.name: Level Look
runners_data.note: Andrew Balding's 3-year-old is a hold-up horse returning from a 189-day absence, having won on his last start at Sandown over 1m2f — the step to 1m4f is an open question; David Probert takes the ride and Balding's yard is in fair form at T14:11/56, but the lengthy layoff is the key concern.

runners_data.name: Cranachan
runners_data.note: Ralph Beckett's progressive 3-year-old holds the most solid recent credentials in the field, having won over 1m2f on good ground and placed over 1m4f on similar ground (sim-going: 1W1P); races held up by nature, so depends on Patrol setting enough of a gallop, and the blinkers (hg:b) suggest connections are trying to sharpen his response.

runners_data.name: Counter Intuitive
runners_data.note: Ed Walker's lightly-raced 3-year-old comes here on the back of a career-best effort — a 1m2f win on good ground — and is stepping up in trip for the first time; races prominently and Billy Loughnane will look to track Patrol closely, giving him a tactical advantage over the pure hold-up horses if the pace is modest.

races.paceDynamic: Patrol is the lone confirmed pace-setter in this four-runner field and should dictate from the front over 1m4f on good ground at Newmarket's July course, setting a sustainable rhythm with no pressure from behind. Counter Intuitive carries a prominent tag but is a 3-year-old with limited experience, and is unlikely to challenge Patrol for the lead, instead settling just off the pace. Level Look and Cranachan are both hold-up horses who will be anchored at the rear, relying on a strong gallop to close into. With a single, uncontested leader setting a measured pace over this stamina trip, the race shape is likely to suit hold-up horses who can produce a sustained late run, though the lack of genuine pressure on Patrol means those closers may need to work hard to reel in a well-positioned leader — making the profile of a horse that can travel prominently and pick up off the pace the most dangerous.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Patrol Controls, Stays On
scenarios.trigger: If Patrol dictates an uncontested, measured gallop and proves good enough over this trip.
scenarios.body: Patrol leads throughout, sets a comfortable pace and, never headed, conserves enough energy to repel challengers in the closing stages; at 1m4f on good ground with no rival willing to pressurise, the front-runner's chance is maximised. Counter Intuitive, racing prominently just behind, is best placed to chase Patrol home if the closers struggle to get to them.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Closers Swoop Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough that Patrol empties late and the hold-up horses finish with purpose.
scenarios.body: Cranachan and Level Look, tracking from the rear, need Patrol to stretch the field at a clip that leaves him vulnerable inside the final two furlongs; Cranachan's good-ground form is solid (1W1P in 2 sim-going runs) and Hector Crouch will look to deliver a sustained challenge from off the pace.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Dominate
scenarios.trigger: If Counter Intuitive improves past Patrol to lead and the pair fight out the finish ahead of the closers.
scenarios.body: Billy Loughnane on Counter Intuitive, a winner last time out over 1m2f on good ground, may push forward to press Patrol, turning the race into a two-horse battle that leaves the hold-up horses with too much ground to make up. Ed Walker's 3-year-old is unexposed at this trip and could find improvement.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Long-Run Stamina Test
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses mid-race and one runner produces a sustained, grinding burst from 3f out.
scenarios.body: An unlikely shape in a race with only four runners and a genuine front-runner, but if Cranachan or Level Look makes an unusually early move to challenge Patrol, the race could become a stamina grind that the most staying-bred 3-year-old wins; Cranachan's best form has come over 1m4f-1m2f on good ground.

watchPoints.text: If Patrol is allowed to bowl along completely unchallenged through the early and middle stages, watch for him to prove very hard to peg back at this trip — Counter Intuitive must decide early whether to press or concede the lead.

Cranachan's blinkers are a flag — connections have added headgear for the first time, suggesting he may have been held up too far back in recent runs; watch how sharply Hector Crouch sends him through the field once the tempo lifts.

Level Look's 189-day absence is the biggest unknown in the race — watch his paddock condition and early movement carefully, as Balding horses can need a run on return and the drop from a month's prep to a race-day test can expose ring rust.

With only four runners, any significant market move for Cranachan or Counter Intuitive in the hour before post time should be noted — in a small field, late money often reflects stable confidence about fitness or going suitability that is not visible in the form book.

races.name: National Stud Handicap Stakes (GBBPlus Race)

runners_data.name: High Degree
runners_data.note: William Haggas's four-year-old is the sole natural front-runner and effectively guaranteed the lead under Fallon; his sim-going record of 7/9 on good is solid, though his form string (46-235) shows he has been beaten consistently at this level — the question is whether uncontested control at this trip is enough.|

runners_data.name: Al Aali
runners_data.note: George Scott's gelding has a dismal recent profile over 10-12f on good ground (five runs, no wins or places at sim-going 7/15), and the hood he carries has not sparked improvement; Billy Loughnane will likely track the midfield but this horse is yet to demonstrate he belongs at this level over this trip.|

runners_data.name: Way Of Life
runners_data.note: Jonathan Portman's eight-year-old is a course-specialist on synthetic surfaces (three wins at Wolverhampton, one at Lingfield) and his only good-ground 12f run produced a fifth; Olivia Tubb's 5lb claim helps the weight, but 81 days off the track and unproven form on turf at Newmarket are legitimate reservations.|

runners_data.name: Percy's Daydream
runners_data.note: David O'Meara's four-year-old boasts the most convincing pace-on-good profile in the race (11/13 sim-going, four wins at 10-12f) and is a natural front-runner who will find himself shuffled into a midfield berth against his instincts — Probert will need a clean run to compensate for the compromised position.|

runners_data.name: War Hawk
runners_data.note: Simon & Ed Crisford's gelding returns after 126 days off and is fitted with a tongue-tie — the layoff is the obvious concern, though Crisford's T14 strike rate (6/24) suggests they know when a horse is ready; he too is a genuine prominent type who will likely race off the pace through no choice of his own.|

runners_data.name: Darn Hot Gallop
runners_data.note: James Tate's three-year-old is tackling 1m2f for the first time after consecutive wins over 7-8f on faster ground, which makes stamina a real unknown; he carries a featherweight 129lbs and, while naturally a forward-going type, will find himself racing in unfamiliar territory both tactically and in terms of trip.|

races.paceDynamic: High Degree is the lone confirmed front-runner here and, with only six runners over 1m2f at Newmarket, is virtually certain to stride into a clear lead from the outset with Cieren Fallon dictating a controlled, sustainable gallop — there is no natural rival to press him. The field behind him is crowded with prominent types: War Hawk, Percy's Daydream, and Darn Hot Gallop are all genuine up-with-the-pace horses who cannot all occupy that position and are therefore mapped into a congested midfield, where they will race against their instincts. Way Of Life and Al Aali, both capable of racing prominently or off the pace, are likely to fill the chasing positions, but the tactical picture is one of a modest, unhurried tempo set by a horse racing comfortably within himself. This shape — a steady pace, a compressed midfield pack racing out of role, and a clear leader who reaches the home turn unflustered — favours a well-positioned horse with a strong turn-of-foot who can accelerate off a slow tempo, or indeed the leader himself if the gallop is too gentle to bring the closers into play.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Leader Dictates Unchallenged
scenarios.trigger: If High Degree controls an uncontested pace and the compressed midfield fails to organise a meaningful challenge turning in.
scenarios.body: High Degree, allowed to bowl along at a comfortable clip with Fallon judging every furlong, reaches the straight with a decisive lead and enough petrol left to repel the mid-pack surge; the prominent types stuck racing wide or out of position lose their winning rhythm before the race ignites.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Type Pounces Late
scenarios.trigger: If one of the redistributed prominent horses — most likely Percy's Daydream or War Hawk — secures a handy position just off the leader and pings clear entering the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Percy's Daydream has the strongest pace-to-ground credentials in this field (11/13 sim-going, four wins) and, if David Probert gets him slotted just off High Degree, he can use his natural forward-going energy to pick off the leader; War Hawk, fresh from 126 days off and fitted with a tongue-tie, is the secondary threat if Simon & Ed Crisford have him sharp.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Sweeps Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses late and Al Aali or Way Of Life finds a gap as the leaders tie up in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Al Aali has gone well enough on good ground over 12f before and Billy Loughnane could produce him with a late run if the congested midfield splits; Way Of Life's record of three wins over 10-11f on Stansted going and a recent 1/12f win shows she stays strongly, and Olivia Tubb (claiming 5lb) keeps the weight competitive.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Darn Hot Gallop Delivers Shock
scenarios.trigger: If Darn Hot Gallop, dropping in class and attempting 1m2f for the first time, finds the step up in trip unlocking improvement and threads through late.
scenarios.body: James Tate's three-year-old has won twice over 7-8f on fast ground and carries a featherweight 129lbs, and if the extra distance reveals untapped stamina he could sprint past a tiring field; however, his redistribution from his natural prominent role and unproven stamina beyond a mile make this the longest of shots.

watchPoints.text: High Degree is the only horse guaranteed the lead — if Fallon slows the pace to a crawl in the straight, this becomes a sprint and the backmarkers lose any chance of getting involved.

Percy's Daydream, War Hawk and Darn Hot Gallop are all natural front-runners who cannot all hold their preferred position; watch for scrimmaging and shuffling in the first two furlongs as they jockey for ground they cannot all secure.

War Hawk's 126-day absence is the longest layoff in the field — monitor him in the pre-parade for any signs of fitness or saddling issues that would further diminish his chance on a compromised run-style day.

Way Of Life's entire win record is on artificial surfaces; if the Newmarket turf is riding with any cut or pace, her ability to transfer that form to good ground at 1m2f here is unproven and worth treating with caution.

Al Aali has failed to place in five consecutive runs on good going over 10-12f — his sim-going conversion rate (7/15, 0W0P) is the weakest in the field and his chance depends heavily on the shape of the race breaking unusually in his favour.

races.name: Madness Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Rocking Ends
runners_data.note: Sole front-runner on confirmed form, Good ground suits (13/15 sim-going record), visor retained, fresh on 7-day turnaround — Tom Clover in fair recent form and Cieren Fallon a booking upgrade, though the style-fit flag suggests this is not his natural lead role.|

runners_data.name: Valley Ofthe Kings
runners_data.note: Drops back from 6f to 5f which is a concern given all five recorded runs are over 6f or further; George Wood rides and similar going record is modest at 4/15 — needs to prove the shorter trip does not leave him flat.|

runners_data.name: Grandlad
runners_data.note: Won last time out over this exact trip on Good ground and brings the most relevant form in the field; 82-day absence is the key risk alongside James Horton's quiet recent run of 0W from 6 — tongue tie retained and hold-up style suits if pace is adequate.|

runners_data.name: Rogue Bullet
runners_data.note: Prominent racer who won over 6f on Good and placed over 5f on Good — Billy Loughnane's record in this type of race is worth noting, and James Owen's yard is running at 8/47 in the 14-day window, suggesting some activity and confidence.|

runners_data.name: Diomed Duke
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up type who places repeatedly at this trip on Good ground (five of last five on Good or Soft); 27-day break is not a concern given Stuart Williams' handling of him, though OR of 72 leaves him with ground to find.|

runners_data.name: Tuscan Point
runners_data.note: Comes into this race having won over 5f on Standard and placed at 5f on Good — however, as a true hold-up horse redistributed into the midfield map position, he is structurally unlikely to get his favoured ground-eating finish in a steady-pace race, and the 0.92 style-fit rating reflects that discount.|

runners_data.name: Travel Agent
runners_data.note: Back-to-back wins in recent form but those came at 6f on Standard — the 5f trip on Good is a different challenge entirely, and as a genuine hold-up type pushed forward on the map, the race shape here does not naturally set up for his finishing style despite the lively recent form string.|

runners_data.name: Ecclefechan
runners_data.note: Alice Bond's 5lb claim may partially offset the OR reality; a 3-year-old stepping into this company with six runs showing no win and a best of 4th, all form at 6f-7f on Good — the drop to 5f is unproven and the redistribution from hold-up to midfield maps the structural challenge clearly.|

races.paceDynamic: Rocking Ends is the sole confirmed front-runner in this 5f heat and should bowl along uncontested from the gates, setting a sustainable but not suicidal gallop on Good ground. Valley Of The Kings and Rogue Bullet will press from prominent positions, but neither is a natural front-runner and neither looks likely to seriously challenge Rocking Ends for the lead early. This creates a controlled, single-pace scenario where the tempo is dictated from one source rather than a contested battle — a shape that has historically rewarded horses racing close to the pace who can sustain their effort through the final furlong. The field holds more hold-up types than can be genuinely accommodated at the rear: Tuscan Point, Travel Agent and Ecclefechan are true hold-up horses redistributed into midfield on the map because the real back positions are over-subscribed, meaning they are unlikely to be producing late flourishes from where they want to be. The tactical verdict is clear: a steady, uncontested pace favours prominent racers who travel close to the lead and stay on — not hold-up horses who need a strong gallop to pull them through a weakening field.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Rocking Ends Controls Uncontested
scenarios.trigger: If Rocking Ends leads comfortably and sets a steady gallop with no serious early challenger, the race becomes a test of stamina and rail position rather than finishing kick.
scenarios.body: Rocking Ends dictates from flag to line, the pace never truly increases to punish him, and close-travelling prominent types who conserve energy early benefit most in the final furlong.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Pair Grind It Out
scenarios.trigger: If Valley Of The Kings and Rogue Bullet track Rocking Ends closely and the pace is honest enough to stretch the field but not collapse the leaders.
scenarios.body: The race develops into a tight, grinding finish between the prominent quartet, with Rogue Bullet's 5f course form and Grandlad's recent winning run over the distance placing them well.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Bursts Through
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is surprisingly strong and creates enough gaps for a late runner to pick off tiring horses in the final 100 yards.
scenarios.body: Grandlad, who is the most genuine of the hold-up types on raw form and won last time over this exact trip on Good ground, is best placed to exploit; the redistributed Tuscan Point and Travel Agent are less likely to achieve their natural positions and are structurally disadvantaged in this shape.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Race Falls Apart Chaos
scenarios.trigger: If multiple horses break poorly or there is interference early, scrambling the pace and negating the natural order entirely.
scenarios.body: Unpredictable positioning benefits unexposed or lightly handicapped types like Ecclefechan who may find a seam from whatever position they land, though their form in this company is not compelling.

watchPoints.text: Grandlad's 82-day absence is the single most important unknown — if he returns fit, his 5f Good winning form is the most directly relevant in the race and he becomes a major factor in any scenario.

Travel Agent and Tuscan Point both trained by Adam Kirby (0W from 16 in the 14-day window) — stable in a quiet spell and neither horse is likely to be racing from their preferred position, which compounds the concern.
Valley Of The Kings has run exclusively at 6f and beyond — watch the market closely; if support dries up before the off, the trip drop is likely catching up with punters.

Rogue Bullet is drawn and ridden by Billy Loughnane, who excels at 5f and on Good ground at this level — monitor whether he tries to take a closer position than his OR-80 placing would suggest, as that could compress the prominent group around Rocking Ends.

Ecclefechan is 3 years old in a field of 4-6 year olds and has shown nothing over 5f — watch for whether Alice Bond attempts a covered position to compensate for what looks a stiff ask at the weights and trip.

races.name: Irish Stallion Farms EBF Fillies' Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Rose Of Honour
runners_data.note: Has won three of her last four — all over 6f on Good or Standard — and James Tate's filly arrives 27 days fresh; she is a natural front-runner who sets the terms here and her recent winning form on comparable going makes her the obvious pace anchor, though her OR of 91 means she carries top weight.

runners_data.name: Novamay
runners_data.note: Michael Dods' four-year-old scored on Soft over 6f last time and has solid similar-going credentials (13 runs, three wins, six places), but her natural desire to race prominently cannot be satisfied in this configuration — she will be forced further back than ideal, which compromises her chance in the most likely race shape.

runners_data.name: Elara May
runners_data.note: 259 days off the track is the headline concern for Philip McBride's three-year-old, though her form of 1-1-3-1 shows a filly who performs; she is a natural prominent racer on Good ground (6/9 similar-going record) and the trip and surface are right, so the bounce risk is the key question mark.

runners_data.name: Angel Shared
runners_data.note: Steph Hollinshead's five-year-old has a modest recent sequence (-75306) and her similar-going figures (11/15) suggest she rarely wins in these conditions; a genuine hold-up type who needs the pace to collapse — possible only in Scenario B — to make her ground.

runners_data.name: Lady Kodiac
runners_data.note: Won over 6f on Standard last time out and has placed twice on Good, making her a legitimate each-way player in the prominent-chaser scenario; Ray Dawson rides for James Tate's yard, and the 29-day break looks routine rather than a concern.

runners_data.name: Powdering
runners_data.note: Billy Loughnane partners this six-year-old who won over 6f on Good ground just 21 days ago — Michael Herrington's stable is in form (4/13 14-day strike rate) and she is the most interesting hold-up type if the pace does unravel; her similar-going record is thin (5/15) but her recent winning run is the live angle.

runners_data.name: Shallow
runners_data.note: George Wood rides a true hold-up performer with strong placed form on Good ground (2-3-3-2 from recent 6f-7f starts), but visor headgear noted and only 6 days since last run raises freshness questions; mapped to midfield against her natural style, she needs a contested tempo that this race shape is unlikely to provide.

runners_data.name: Sing The Blues
runners_data.note: Cieren Fallon partners the Martin Dunne three-year-old returning after 251 days off — her last run was a P (pulled up) and the long absence plus uncertain fitness make this a speculative reappearance; she is at heart a prominent racer who will not get that position here, making her chance doubly complicated.

races.paceDynamic: Rose Of Honour is the confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine challenger likely to contest her lead, she should be able to set a controlled, sustainable gallop from the front at her own terms. Elara May and Lady Kodiac are the other naturally prominent types capable of sitting just off her heels, giving the race a steady but orderly early tempo rather than a contested burn. This field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their preferred position — Novamay and Sing The Blues are genuine up-with-the-pace horses who are likely to find themselves shuffled into a midfield berth against their instincts, while Shallow similarly will not get the true hold-up run it needs. A controlled early fractions on Good ground over 6f at Newmarket's July Course — a track where front-runners with a turn of foot hold a structural advantage — means the race shape strongly favours prominent racers who can sit close to the uncontested leader and produce a clean finishing effort, rather than those coming from off the pace against a tempo that never truly injures the leaders.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Rose Dictates, Prominent Wins
scenarios.trigger: If Rose Of Honour controls a measured gallop and prominent chasers like Elara May and Lady Kodiac track her into the straight.
scenarios.body: Rose Of Honour sets an uncontested, sustainable pace and the prominent chasers have a clean run to the line on a track that rewards those close to the early action; the closing burst from off the pace is blunted because the tempo never truly tests the leaders' stamina.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Hotts Up, Closers Land
scenarios.trigger: If Novamay forces a faster early pace by pushing to the front against her mapped position, stretching the field and burning off the leaders.
scenarios.body: A contested pace collapses the leaders late, opening the door for genuine hold-up types further back; Powdering, who won over this C&D trip on Good ground recently, is ideally placed to reel them in.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front-Runner Wires Field
scenarios.trigger: If Rose Of Honour is allowed to bowl clear on a genuinely easy lead and the chasing pack burns energy closing a gap that never quite disappears.
scenarios.body: With no pressure applied to Rose Of Honour, she simply keeps extending into the Newmarket straight and holds every rival at bay; horses with strong front-running form on similar going like Elara May may grab second but the winner is already gone.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Redistribution Chaos, Upset
scenarios.trigger: If the compressed mid-pack of reluctant hold-up types creates scrimmaging and the race falls apart for the prominent horses.
scenarios.body: Disruption in the main pack costs the favoured prominent types their clear run, gifting a long-odds hold-up specialist a clear path; this is the least likely shape given how few true closers are in the field and their modest recent form.

watchPoints.text: Rose Of Honour sets the fractions entirely on her own terms — if Hector Crouch is allowed to dictate a slow-to-moderate pace, the closing sectionals will be insufficient to peg her back.

Novamay and Sing The Blues are both genuine prominent types forced into midfield by the race configuration — watch for early crowding or position-seeking that could disrupt the pack in the first two furlongs.
Elara May's 259-day absence is the single biggest unknown in the race; if she returns fully wound up she could be a major player, but a flat reappearance after that layoff would not be surprising.

Powdering is the most interesting hold-up horse in the field given her recent 6f Good-ground win and live trainer form — her chance is scenario-dependent but worth monitoring if the early pace is stronger than expected.

Shallow runs just 6 days after her last outing and wears a visor — watch how she travels in the early stages, as a hold-up horse forced wider in midfield with short recovery time is a combination that can produce unpredictable running.

races.name: Burwell Apprentice Handicap Stakes

runners_data.name: Born A Rebel
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer with placed form over this exact 7f trip on good ground and a clean recent run 27 days ago; sits highest in the handicap among the closers and Arron D'Arcy's 7lb claim keeps the weight manageable, though Patrick Owens's yard is cold at 0/3 over the past fortnight.

runners_data.name: Alafdhal
runners_data.note: Aged eight with declining form showing a string of poor finishes, primarily on faster artificial surfaces at shorter trips of 5-6f; a true closer by nature, he will be squeezed into a more forward position than suits him in this single-pace shape, and the step up to 7f on turf looks an additional ask.

runners_data.name: Sedgemoor
runners_data.note: Headgear flagged; John Ryan's yard has a runner in Chloe's Courage in the same race, creating a potential stable-mate dynamic; naturally wants to be dropped in last and delivered late, but with so many genuine closers in this field he will struggle to find his preferred pitch, and his going form on good turf is limited at just one placed run from 15.

runners_data.name: Chloe's Courage
runners_data.note: Returns from a lengthy 176-day absence for the same John Ryan yard and, despite course form over this trip, the lack of a prep run is a significant concern; at her best she is a patient hold-up type with three placed efforts over 7f on Tapeta, but she will be forced forward out of role in this compressed shape.

runners_data.name: Coolagh Magic
runners_data.note: Ten-year-old veteran who most recently won over 6f on good ground and carries a tongue-tie; his best form is on good going and he has solid place percentage in similar conditions, but he too is a natural closer who will be mapped into midfield and asked to race more prominently than he prefers.

runners_data.name: Prefer The Sister
runners_data.note: In excellent form with two wins and four placings from six recent starts, all on good ground and covering both 7f and 8f, making her the classiest closer in the field by recent output; Mason Paetel rides without a claim but James Owen's yard is firing at an 8/47 two-week strike rate, and her headgear combination of hood and tongue-tie is proven — she looks the most likely to find the lead runner from second or third.

runners_data.name: Mister Mojito
runners_data.note: The lone front-runner who sets the entire tactical context of this race; headgear flagged with a tongue-tie, and he has consistent form over this 7f trip on good going with course experience, though a STYLE_FIT flag notes he will be racing in a role slightly out of his natural profile and TJ Kent's yard is winless in five over the past fortnight.

races.paceDynamic: Mister Mojito is the sole confirmed front-runner in this seven-horse field and should stride to the front from the gates, setting a controlled, uncontested gallop over the Newmarket July course seven furlongs. With no other genuine pace-maker to push him, he is unlikely to be pressured into an unsustainable tempo, meaning the race will likely be run at a measured rhythm that keeps the field compressed and bunched behind him for much of the journey. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than the pace map can accommodate at the rear — Alafdhal, Sedgemoor, Chloe's Courage and Coolagh Magic are all genuine closers who are likely to be forced into unnatural, more forward positions than they would naturally seek. This controlled, single-pace shape with a compressed field behind a lone leader most strongly favours horses who can race prominently off the pace or produce a sustained finish from a midfield berth — runners with tactical versatility and proven form on good ground at this trip will be best placed.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Mojito Dictates Solo
scenarios.trigger: If Mister Mojito leads throughout at a controlled gallop and no challenger applies meaningful pressure until the final two furlongs.
scenarios.body: Mister Mojito sets a sustainable pace that flatters his stamina and denies hold-up horses a strong enough tempo to pick them off; horses who can race in second or third and challenge over the final furlong are ideally positioned.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Late Finisher Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is genuinely strong enough in the final two furlongs to stretch the field and allow a closing run from the rear.
scenarios.body: A genuine pace injection late in the race creates space for a horse with a sustained finish to pick up the stragglers, rewarding any runner able to find clear daylight on the outside.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Compressed Midfield Scrap
scenarios.trigger: If several redistributed hold-up types crowd the midfield and the race develops into a bunched sprint from two furlongs out.
scenarios.body: With multiple closers forced forward and jostling for position in an unnatural role, the race degenerates into a flat-out sprint finish from the home turn, suiting those with tactical speed and course experience.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse Carnage
scenarios.trigger: If Mister Mojito stops sharply in the final furlong having front-run too keenly, opening the door for a late pounce from whatever finisher has cover.
scenarios.body: A sudden deceleration in the closing stages creates a vacuum that any horse with residual energy can fill, turning the result on its head entirely.

watchPoints.text: Prefer The Sister is the most in-form horse in the race with her 8/47 trainer strike rate, proven good-ground 7f form and recent race fitness — if she gets a clean passage tracking Mister Mojito she is the primary threat to all outcomes.

Mister Mojito's ability to sustain his lead-setting role is the pivot of the entire race shape — if he fades sharply inside the final furlong, the result becomes unpredictable and any runner with residual energy benefits disproportionately.

The cluster of redistributed closers — Alafdhal, Sedgemoor, Chloe's Courage and Coolagh Magic — all competing for space in an unnatural midfield position creates significant traffic risk in the straight; watch for interference around the two-furlong marker.

Chloe's Courage returns from 176 days off track without a prep run — if she shows any signs of ring-rustiness early it will confirm she needs the run, but if she travels well within the first three furlongs she could be more of a factor than her layoff suggests.
John Ryan saddles two runners (Sedgemoor and Chloe's Courage) in the same race — monitor market moves on both in the final hour before post time for any stable pointer.
